items.text: The Fledglings
Beach, Bay Shore Town, 1969
Birds swoop out over the water, flying east over the crashing waves.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: You know, the papers love writing crazy headlines about Florida.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Like "Ghost Ship Returns from the Atlantic," "Lost War Plane Guided Home by Little Green Men," "Winged Man Lands on Tampa Beach" ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I have heard them before. Our colleagues sometimes share their favorites over lunch.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They would laugh so hard they spilled their coffee.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It was always a mess afterward.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: They say it's the "Devil's Triangle" three points between our coast, Puerto Rico, and Bermuda.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I never considered them credible.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The waters in this so-called triangle are no more treacherous or magical than any other. People should be careful about separating truth from superstition.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I do not doubt that you are more than capable of that.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Of course I can, but, I mean, that last story, I guess I want it to be true. What if it is?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I see. So, you believe that a winged human appeared from the Atlantic and landed here?

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Well, it's just that after you gave me that draft from Uncle Victor.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: At first, I thought we'd never get any further than he did, but when I saw that, I thought maybe we can do it. Maybe it was fate?
Fate. Fate has no direction in her view. Ascribing purpose or intention to a chain of events was just a flaw in human reasoning.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I never considered that.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I had insufficient time to work on it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, I gave it to you. That is all.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Where your uncle failed, I had hoped you might succeed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There was no notion of destiny. I simply made a practical decision.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And this winged man story is just sensationalist journalism. It was a coincidence.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Say what you will. You may not believe in fate, but plenty of others, humans and arcanists alike, do.

items.speaker: Joanna
items.text: Anyway, fate or not, you should see how far we've come.

branch.speaker: Student II
branch.text: That makes it one minute and eight seconds! I win!

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Give me a break. That was one minute and one second! You were still on the ground when you started counting!

branch.speaker: Student II
branch.text: Yeah, because we agreed to start counting as soon as the engine starts!

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: That would be unwise. It is more useful to count only after you have achieved lift-off.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Otherwise, your records may not accurately show your progress, sending you down the wrong path.
The boys turn to the source of the stern yet encouraging voice.

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Wait, it's that robot from before! Cool!

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Hey, everyone! Ms. Joanna brought the robot here!

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Do you mean that your flight duration now exceeds a minute without aid from arcane skills? Simply astounding.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: You should be saying thanks. It was Ms. Lucy who gave us the original prototype for our wings.

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Of course, thanks, Miss!

branch.speaker: Student II
branch.text: Yeah, thanks, Miss Robot!

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: You've correctly guessed our biggest obstacle: fuel.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: We tried enlarging the tank, but the heavier the weight in fuel and material, the less efficient it became. We just can't find a solution that allows for prolonged independent flight.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: But we're still confident, aren't we, gentlemen?

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: It's far from perfect now, but that's fine. As you said, it's only a matter of time, and these kids have plenty of that.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Think how far they'll have progressed by the time they reach my age. The world could be completely different, even from our wildest dreams.
The march of progress has been undeniable, even contained to just the last century. From whale oil lamps and coal, to gasoline and atomic energy, it is hard to imagine what will come next.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: The television is a great example. It has only been around for 44 years. When it first released, it seemed as though it would never dethrone the cinema.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Now it is a staple of modern life. People can hardly spend a day without their favorite shows.

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Are you talking about TV shows? Hey Miss, do you know Captain James T. Kirk and Spock?

branch.speaker: Student II
branch.text: Why did you ask her? It's a TV show, not real life, doofus. She's a robot, not an actress!

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Yeah, I know she's a robot! That's why I figured she'd have to know about the best sci-fi show of all time.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Let's stop pestering Miss Lucy about her favorite shows, alright boys? Unless, you'd like to spend tomorrow cleaning out the school swimming pool?

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Sound like fun to you?
It is a half-joking threat, but enough to bring the boys in line.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: That would be quite a shame. You would very likely miss the broadcast.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I am very proud to say it is LSCC technology that was pivotal in constructing the signal-boosting devices.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: But for now, let me see the problem that you have been dealing with.
The mechanical woman walks toward the metal construct lying in the sand.

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Daniel and Annie and the others helped us move it out here.

branch.speaker: Student II
branch.text: Yeah. We promised them everyone would get a try after we've ironed out the kinks.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: We've hit a hard limit now; I've tried everything I could think of to help them.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: One minute is already a remarkable achievement. Is this why you invited me here?

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Well, that and I miss working with you, Lucy.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: The switch was worth it, believe me. Still, I do miss some parts of my career, and my colleagues.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: So, think you can lend us a hand?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I will attempt to do so. Is it still powered by liquid fuel?

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Until recently it was. We've actually been getting it straight from the Space Center. So, it was about as high-grade as you can get.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: But, we've been toying with something else now. To cut the weight down, we switched to wired electricity.
Lucy scans over the beach, finding a long black cord connected from the machine back toward a nearby generator.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: A wire? That completely restricts your flight range.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: The length of the cord would determine your maximum radius.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: You have created an electric kite.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: At least we replaced the thread with a wire.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: But you're right. It's nothing more than a kind of powered kite. They even call it that sometimes. But what else can we do?

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: This was the only solution that gave us any kind of stable flight.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Once unplugged, the battery can only sustain the engine for less than a minute.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I see. So, it is not a matter of fuel, but rather of capacity.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: A simple adjustment will resolve this issue.
She produces a silvery metallic block from her coat, an emergency power source, made from the miraculous fusion of arcanum and material science.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: If your design has a T-2 general slot, this battery may work as a substitute.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Let me try.
She skillfully replaces the battery.
Then unplugs the wings.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Try it again.

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: So, what is it? A new battery?

branch.speaker: Student I
branch.text: Is that going to be enough?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I am confident it will dramatically improve your flight time.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: However, I suggest you do not fly too high or too far away from the beach, at least until we know the precise power draw.
Joanna and the students crowd around the wings to see the new component.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: I didn't know the Space Center had been working on battery technology.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Actually, this is a product I developed with the LSCC in 1965.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: An arcanist colleague there helped me complete this project. The arcanum imbued in it should allow it to ignore the usual physical limits of its material.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: I can only imagine what could be done with technology like that. Has it been released?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: We have begun mass production. We are only waiting for official permission to make it publicly available.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: By harnessing arcanum, we were able to achieve a similar energy density to rocket fuel, but without the need for cumbersome tanks and piping.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Petroleum was a marvel of science that laid the foundation for modern civilization. That being the case, I believe that if arcane skills could be studied comprehensively and replicated, they might be capable of supplanting fossil fuel entirely.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: I always thought you refused to use arcane skills to enhance technology?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I opposed the use of arcane skill only because it was unstable and not replicable at scale.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: However, if it can be incorporated into technology in a controllable and generalized way, it can work.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: The gap between arcane skills and human technologies is really not so different, no more than that between a human brain and a computer.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: One is created through genetic coding, while the other is created by digital coding. They are essentially the same.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: If it were anyone else saying that, I'd have called them a nut job.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Why?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: A fact remains a fact, regardless of who says it.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: And a mechanical device has the same function, no matter its user.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: That much is true. But we're getting ahead of ourselves. We still need to see the results of our test flight.
In a short time, the first brave pilot takes off on his aluminum wings. The students cheer as the stopwatch counts up to 60 seconds and then beyond.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: It seems like a remarkable success.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: This will be the end of an era. No more competition. Just fun.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: I think we can call our project completed.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Well, only thanks to you.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Do you want me to report this achievement to the Space Center? Or maybe the LSCC.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Not quite yet. There's still room for improvement. So how long do you think that battery can last now?

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: We will need to do further testing to determine that; however, I suspect it is an improvement by orders of magnitude.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Then maybe I should call him down. Just to be safe.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: Jack, get down here. Danny, Peter, please clear the beach off for landing.
Reluctantly, the young man returns from the sky, making a steady landing on the sand.

branch.speaker: Lucy
branch.text: Ten minutes and 48 seconds. That makes for quite a new record.

branch.speaker: Joanna
branch.text: I'm certain they'll have beat that handily before you know it.
